recipes.name: Cavatelli and Broccoli
ingredients_raw: 3 heads fresh broccoli, cut into florets
1 teaspoon salt, or more to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook broccoli in boiling water for about 5 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to remove broccoli to a large bowl and set aside.
Season boiling water in the same pot with salt. Cook cavatelli in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bite, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté garlic in hot oil until lightly golden, being careful not to burn it. Add broccoli; cook, stirring occasionally, until tender yet crisp to the bite, about 10 minutes.
Add cooked cavatelli to the skillet; toss well with broccoli mixture until warmed through. Season with salt and hot pepper flakes. Serve with Parmesan cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Cavatelli and Broccoli
raw_recipe.description: This cavatelli and broccoli dish features blanched florets sautéed in garlicky olive oil, then tossed with hot pasta, red pepper flakes, and Parmesan.

review.reviewBody: This is a very good dish if you make it the right way. I think other members have commented on this, but i'll reiterate. You have to put (depending on how much you make, I usually make it with 2 bags of cavatellis) about a regular coffee mug size amount of the salted pasta water into the broccoli pan, then drain the pasta, then put the pasta into the pan with the broccoli and let it cook for a few more minutes. I guarantee this will make it taste a whole lot better, since when the cavatelli's cook in the broccoli for a bit they soak up the flavor. Hope this helps!

This was a really great recipe!

I used a 1/4C of olive oil and 1 Tablespoon of unsalted butter-added my own seasonings like I do in all recipes. I added seasoned salt, Italian seasoning and a sprinkling of kosher salt, not regular salt. 
I liberally salted the pasta water with kosher salt and reserved some of the pasta water to add to the sauce. I also added a little olive oil as needed while cooking to adjust the moisture of the dish. I think adding some chicken or shrimp to this would be awesome too.
I served a tomato, cucumber and onion salad on the side with a homemade dressing of olive oil, red wine vinegar, kosher salt and fresh crushed black pepper. This added a burst of color and freshness to this dish.
This will definitely be placed in my rotation of recipes.

I sautéed the broccoli in minced garlic and other spices for taste. I then added the noodles, broccoli, and vegan cheese into a tin and baked. It has tons of flavor thanks to other reviews saying to boil in salted water. Delicious

Salt the water with 1T, saute 4 cloves of garlic in butter, add 1-2 cups of pasta water to the broccoli, and increase the parmesan cheese. I also added 1 jar artichoke hearts with some of the pickling juice, 1 T Italian seasoning and 1 T Seasoned Salt. I would not blanch the broccoli prior to sauteeing. I prefer my broccoli to have some crunch and the parboiling made it fall apart.

I just blanched a small head of broccoli, cooked 1/2 c of mini rigatoni, 1/4 c of grape tomatoes halved . I used 2T olive oil & stirred everything together in a covered microwave dish & cooked for 2 min. When it was done, I sprinkled it with Parmesan Cheese. Just right for one person.

I use a wok since I make a large portion (3 bags of frozen broccoli florets and 2 bags of cavatelli). I steam the broccoli in the microwave first. In a wok I sauté the garlic and red pepper flakes. Then throw the steamed broccoli in. When broccoli is done, I zest one lemon and squeeze the juice of the lemon into the broccoli. Then I throw the cooked cavatelli into the wok and mix it all up and cook for a few minutes longer. The lemon gives it a really good flavor.

Here's wha6t I did, cobbling together from the other comments...

Bring chicken stock (about 2 qts) and about 1/4 cup of salt to a boil to blanch your broccoli. Get it to a boil, then submerge the broccoli for 2 minutes AT MOST. Remove it and shock it in cold/ice water. I usually separately cook a package of frozen chopped broccoli (cooked just enough that its not a brick anymore) to add to the mix later.

DON'T DISCARD the water. Set the broccoli aside.

Put 1 lb (2 if you're adventurous) of frozen cavatelli in the broccoli water. Bring to a boil, then boil for about 5-7 minutes (don't cook it till its floppy. It'll continue to cook while you prep the rest of the meal) Set aside. 

Heat 1/4 cup of olive oil in a frying pan. Add to that 3 (hugely heaping) T of minced garlic. Also add 1/4 to 1/2 C of chopped red onion. Sautee over low heat for maybe two minutes, then add the broccoli (and the previously frozen stuff) and sautee for another 4 minutes.

Add 1 cup of the broccoli water (do this earlier if the broccoli or garlic is burning) and sautee.

Sautee for 4 or 5 minutes.

Add the pepper flakes. Or don't. It's already good by itself. Right before serving, add the parmesian cheese and toss.

Enjoy

Ummm...a tsp of salt? 2 tbsp of grated cheese? No way....needs ALOT more. Be sure to add the cheese off of the heat or it gets gummy. Reserve some pasta water to richen the sauce. In place of red pepper flakes I chop up a hot cherry pepper (the kind from the jar) and sauté with the brocolli & garlic. Kicks up the spice a bit & adds some color.
Great dish for a crowd, leftovers, potluck...anything. I added a little white wine, artichoke hearts, sliced green olives and halved cherry tomatoes. We like veggies.

I made this as directed but adding some of the pasta water as other reviewers suggested. The red pepper flakes add heat but not flavor - was sort of bland. I added lemon pepper to my bowl and then was satisfied with that. I will make again but will up the garlic and for myself would add sautéed onions/peppers/mushrooms.

My family has made this recipe since I was a kid. Its super simple and has great flavor if you make it right. My suggestions to make it even easier is to cook the broccoli first in a pot and then add the pasta to the same pot continuing to cook the broccoli so it is well done. When water boils a second time and pasta is cooked (you can use any type of pasta) Cavatelli can take longer to cook. Strain the water and put it into a serving bowl. In a separate pot, saute the chopped garlic (always use fresh garlic) and when it starts to brown and pour it over the pasta and broccoli to serve. Add red pepper and parm cheese to your taste. Its almost a one pot meal this way with easy clean up.

Have been making a variation of this for years. I also add a palmful of lemon pepper seasoning to the oil/ garlic mixture before adding the broccoli and pasta. Reserve some of the pasta water to thicken the sauce and serve with crushed dried red pepper flakes and grated Parmesan cheese.
I added a little chicken broth. While sautéd garlic and broccoli.

I add butter to the oil and garlic, after I add broccoli and cook it in add the pasta, cooking wine, chicken broth and some of the past water. It adds flavor Cover and let simmer. I also melt provolone on top.
It was okay, not much flavor. Even my husband who likes everything thought it was bland. Probably won’t make it again and if I do I would do a lot of tweaking.
Some chicken on the side and let those slice it and put it in them selves and they loved it as well as used a bit more garlic with the broccoli
